newsitem.title: UK: Mervyn King to become second BOE deputy governor.
newsitem.headline: Mervyn King to become second BOE deputy governor.

text.p: The Bank of England said its chief economist Mervyn King would become its second deputy governor alongside the newly appointed David Clementi once the necessary legislation has been passed.

"Following the passage of the Bank of England legislation, which will provide for a second deputy governor, it will be recommended to the Queen that Mervyn King will become the deputy governor supporting the Governor on monetary policy issues," the Bank said in a statement.

King, 49, became executive director and chief economist at the Bank on March 1, 1991 having previously been a non-executive director since 1990. From 1984 to 1991, he was professor of economics at the London School of Economics.

The Bank's biographical sketch said King "would like to spend more time reading European history, listening to music and playing tennis, which he did regularly before the inflation target was introduced."
